#16 This result is only true when also a terminal object exists. For example, the empty category is locally cartesian closed and has coequalizers, but it is not regular. A more interesting example is the thin category of natural numbers; it is also locally cartesian closed and has coequalizers, but is not regular.

#17 In the characterisation of regular categories in terms of stable factorisation systems, you do not need to assume that the left maps are regular (rather, this can be deduced). So I changed the text to say “strong” instead of “regular”.
